systems.name: creative-apps
systems.description: The macOS app shells of the creative suite: five SwiftUI apps (Flare, Design, Photo, Library, Halo), each over a Linux-safe Model target, plus the SuiteUI design system.

containers.name: SuiteUI
containers.description: The shared design system (Sources/SuiteUI): tokens, Liquid Glass primitives, the SuiteWindow shell, toolbar palette, sidebar rows and sections, content-layer surfaces, pro inspector rows and scrub fields, a thumbnail grid and a timeline strip. macOS only; knows no Model or engine.

components.name: SuiteUI sources
components.description: The shared design system (Sources/SuiteUI): spacing, radius, size, type and color tokens; Liquid Glass applied in one snapshot-aware place (Glass) and GlassPanel; the SuiteWindow shell (sidebar, content, inspector) with SidebarSection and SidebarRow; ToolbarGroup palette actions; the content layer (CanvasSurface, SurfaceCard, EmptyStateView, ViewerStatusBar); the editor shell after the Ripple editor (EditorShell, EditorTopBar and its bar items, the docked ToolbarGroup rail, CanvasViewport with its Ruler, checkerboard and CanvasMarks, SegmentedTabs and the ColorWell hex row); pro inspector parts (InspectorHeader, InspectorRows, ScrubField and NumericInput number entry); the Studio easing parts (CurveEditor, StudioScrubRow, ChoiceChips); ThumbnailGrid with its selection math; and TimelineStrip with its frame mapping, shared by Flare and Halo.

containers.name: FlareApp
containers.description: The Flare app (2D animation): the SwiftUI App scene and views in Sources/FlareApp, built from SuiteUI. Reads FlareModel and calls its methods; never writes its state (scripts/ci app-state rule).

components.name: FlareApp sources
components.description: The Flare app (2D animation): the SwiftUI App scene, its menu bar (FlareCommands) and views in Sources/FlareApp, including the easing inspector on the live FlareWorkspace, built from SuiteUI.

containers.name: FlareModel
containers.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Flare's window. FlareWorkspace: the open FlareCore document, selected scene and drawing tool. Foundation only, value types.

components.name: FlareModel sources
components.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Flare's window: FlareWorkspace (document, selection, tool, frame and playback, drafts) and FlareServices: the use-case contracts, their live conformances over FlareCore, and the fixture fakes the UI track and snapshots run on. FlareWorkspaceState holds the export, assist and file-load states the workspace stores. FlareFiles opens .flare files through load (progress first, a pure decode the app runs off the main thread, then the landing), hands the app a save's bytes, and keeps the file name, the window title and the dirty flag (the document against the one last opened or saved), with section 3.3's alert text for each FormatError. FlareSelection picks layers or items by click, Shift-click and marquee, and gives the selection box's bounds; FlareDrag turns stage gestures into a draft or move preview and commits each once, on mouse-up, as one named undo step; FlareDrawing adds the Ellipse tool's draft and its one-step commit; FlareScenes adds, renames, removes (never the last), reorders and sets up scenes; FlareGuides adds, moves (one coalesced step per drag), removes and clears ruler guides; FlareEdit runs the Edit menu (Cut, Copy, Paste, Duplicate, Delete, Select All, Deselect), each one named undo step or disabled with the reason it refuses with; FlareAnimate holds auto-key and the inspector's animated properties (Mixed across layers, one coalesced step per scrub, the stopwatch and keyframe button); EasingEditing is the easing editor's contract, which FlareWorkspace conforms to over FlareCore's SetKeyframeEasing, with FakeEasingEditing as its in-memory stand-in for UI work. FlareOnionState holds onion skin and motion path preferences and reads ghosts and the path from services.onion. FlareServices holds one fake per use-case contract (FakeScenes, FakeStage, FakeHits, FakeShapes, FakeProperties with section 2's not-animated rule, FakeKeyframes, FakeEasing, FakeOnion, FakeLibrary, FakeMachines and FakePreview so far, NotBuilt for the rest) over the fixture documents in FlareFixtures (empty, bounce, character, button, button with states and button with machine). FlareSymbols holds the Library tab's symbols and swatches, Convert to Symbol, place, the reason Delete is disabled while a symbol is in use, and editing a symbol in place: the owner switch, the symbol's length on the timeline and the scene frame to return to. MachineLayout lays out a state machine's graph for the Interactions editor: columns by breadth-first distance from the initial state, unreachable states in a last column. FlareMachines holds the Interactions editor's state: the edited machine, states from frame labels, transitions and inputs, each edit one named undo step through services.machines with refusals in machineError, and the live preview over services.preview, which any machine edit stops.

containers.name: DesignApp
containers.description: The Design app (vector and UI design): the SwiftUI App scene and views in Sources/DesignApp, built from SuiteUI's EditorShell. Reads DesignModel and sends it intents through DesignWindow; never writes its state (scripts/ci app-state rule).

components.name: DesignApp sources
components.description: The Design app (vector and UI design): the SwiftUI App scene and views in Sources/DesignApp, built from SuiteUI's EditorShell: the window and its intents (DesignWindow, DesignIntent), the top bar, the tool rail, the canvas with selection handles (drawn above the page clip) and the inline text editor, the Properties | Layers panel (a List of the pages and the layer tree), the File, Edit, Page and View menus, and the open and save panels.

containers.name: DesignModel
containers.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Design's window: pages, the node tree on each page (with fills and text) and which Layers rows are expanded, the selection, the tool, the model-owned undo history, the canvas gestures and the file codec. Foundation only, value types.

components.name: DesignModel sources
components.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Design's window: DesignWorkspace (pages, the selected page and node, the tool, the open file's URL), DesignNode (the node tree on a page, each node with a fill and text, in absolute page points) and the tree flattened into rows under the expanded set, DesignHistory (the model-owned undo and redo, one named step per edit; New File's step carries the replaced document's file URL, which Undo puts back), the canvas gestures (hit testing, the handles a selection shows, draw, move, resize, nudge, delete, in DesignCanvasEditing and DesignDrawing), the inline text edit (DesignText), the inspector's header lines (DesignInspectorContent), the lock that covers a node's subtree and the line saying why (DesignLocking), the Layers row's eye and lock toggles and the hidden-in-tree check (DesignLayerToggles), the held-id index id minting reads (DesignHeldIDs), and the file codec (DesignFile).

containers.name: PhotoApp
containers.description: The Photo app (raster editing): the SwiftUI App scene and views in Sources/PhotoApp, built from SuiteUI. Reads PhotoModel and calls its methods; never writes its state (scripts/ci app-state rule).

components.name: PhotoApp sources
components.description: The Photo app (raster editing): the SwiftUI App scene and views in Sources/PhotoApp, built from SuiteUI's EditorShell: the window and its intents, the top bar, tool rail and canvas (with the Clone tool's Option-click to sample its source and the source's mark), the Adjust | Layers panel (tool options, adjustment sections with the Levels gamma ScrubField and the Curves tone curve over its histogram, the layer list), the export, image size and straighten sheets (the straighten preview turns the canvas picture on the GPU under a grid), the File, Edit, Select, Image, Layer and View menus, the coalescing canvas renderer, the pen pressure read from AppKit mouse events for brush drags, and the ImageIO codec behind PhotoModel's PhotoImageCodec.

containers.name: PhotoModel
containers.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Photo's window: the canvas as a CoreRaster PixelBuffer, its layer stack, selected layer and tool, adjustment settings, and inspector and Layer menu state. Foundation only, value types.

components.name: PhotoModel sources
components.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Photo's window: PhotoWorkspace (the open image's size and name, the layer stack with each layer's offset and its pixels as copy-on-write CoreRaster tiles (TiledPixels), so an edit copies only the tiles it touches, the selected layer, tool, and the brush's and eraser's own tool options with the brush cursor diameter, the marquee selection and pending crop), the tools' drags (brush and eraser dabs, clone, marquee, crop, move), the clone stamp (a sampled source and a stroke that copies from it at a fixed offset onto the selected layer), selection edits and crop, Image Size, Rotate and Straighten (worked out off the main actor, committed unless the image changed), the undo history (the tiles an edit changed, layer lists and whole stacks, read as a list of named steps from "New Image" or "Open" with a jump to any step), the tile-parallel renderer with damage tracking and the adjustments it applies (exposure, levels, curves, hue/saturation, blur) with the curve editor's samples and histogram, opening and exporting through the PhotoImageCodec protocol, the adjustment settings and logarithmic gamma track (with the Gamma field's commit, a no-op for the value it shows), what the inspector shows (with the panel header lines and the viewer status size text), and when each Layer menu item can run (with Bring Forward and Send Backward, one place up or down the stack, and Select Layer Above and Below).

containers.name: LibraryApp
containers.description: The Library app (photo catalog): the SwiftUI App scene and views in Sources/LibraryApp, built from SuiteUI. Reads LibraryModel and calls its methods; never writes its state (scripts/ci app-state rule).

components.name: LibraryApp sources
components.description: The Library app (photo catalog): the SwiftUI App scene and views in Sources/LibraryApp, built from SuiteUI: the window with its thumbnail grid, and the File > Load Sample Photos, View > Sort By and thumbnail size commands.

containers.name: LibraryModel
containers.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Library's window: the catalog's photos, sidebar collections with counts, the selected collection and sort order, and seeded sample photos. Foundation only, value types.

components.name: LibraryModel sources
components.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Library's window: LibraryCatalog (photos, collections with counts, the selected collection, sort order), PhotoItem with its sort orders, and 60 seeded sample photos.

containers.name: HaloApp
containers.description: The Halo app (motion graphics): the SwiftUI App scene and views in Sources/HaloApp, built from SuiteUI. Reads HaloModel and calls its methods; never writes its state (scripts/ci app-state rule).

components.name: HaloApp sources
components.description: The Halo app (motion graphics): the SwiftUI App scene and views in Sources/HaloApp, built from SuiteUI: the window, the Layer and Composition menus, the selected composition's layer list, the New Composition sheet, and the alert for a refused rename.

containers.name: HaloModel
containers.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Halo's window: the project's compositions and their layers, the selected composition, New Composition settings, and refused renames. Foundation only, value types.

components.name: HaloModel sources
components.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Halo's window: HaloProject (compositions, the selected one, unique names), HaloLayer (kind, span, color, opacity, CoreRaster blend mode, solid rectangle), FrameRenderer (composites a composition's solids into one preview frame with CoreRaster), the New Composition draft and its validated settings, and RefusedRename, which keeps a refused composition rename for the alert.
